A1.justification: Despite the new title, v2 describes the same Underload research. Both PDFs are complete and readable; v1 Sections 6–11 correspond to v2 Appendices A–F, with their experiments, figures, and tables retained.

before.justification: v1 reports original defense-accuracy measurements, GPU latency profiling, ablations, sensitivity studies, and DETR/RT-DETR timing experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 3–5 and the supplementary material, including benchmark accuracy and hardware timing measurements.

M1.justification: The objectness-loss proxy, background masking, adversarial-training procedure, and hardware-capacity constraint remain unchanged. Algorithm 2 introduces no new steps or components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PASCAL-VOC, MS-COCO, and BDD100K, with the same hardware environments, semantic examples, and synthetic instance-count scenarios for DETR/RT-DETR. Moving supporting evaluations into appendices does not change coverage.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain Standard, MTD, and OOD under Daedalus, Phantom Sponge, and Overload. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the hyperparameter sweeps and framework timing experiments.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, model variants, mAP50 evaluation, four-step PGD training, perturbation magnitude, and optimizer settings are unchanged. The DETR instance-count tests and ONNX/TensorRT procedures are retained without protocol revisions.

E4.justification: The mask-size ablation, background-semantics cases, training-process analysis, DETR timing analysis, attack-strength sweep, and IoU-threshold sweep all remain. Appendices A–F reorganize existing material rather than introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report five experimental repetitions and 100 inference repetitions for DETR timing. The graphical uncertainty displays are unchanged, with no additional seed information or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The entries in Tables 1–5 match, and all plotted results are retained. For example, Table 1 reports the same YOLOv5s VOC accuracy of 61.3% under Phantom Sponge and 53.3% under Overload for Underload.

T1.justification: The hardware-capacity reasoning, boundary-margin definition, and three stated properties are unchanged. Equation (11) repairs a missing closing parenthesis without changing the intended objective or mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same specialized-defense, hardware-adaptation, and accuracy–robustness claims, including restoring 13 FPS to 43 FPS on Jetson Orin NX. The new title does not redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: The background-vulnerability explanation, mask-size tradeoff, DETR applicability boundary, and low-IoU failure interpretation are retained. Section 5.5 removes its closing future-work sentence but still presents class-specific fine-tuning only as a possibility.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies an Underload source-code URL in the abstract. Existing hardware specifications, software versions, hyperparameters, and framework-export details remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information, not the repository's availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds five citations supporting autonomous-driving, UAV, surveillance/edge-detection applications, and the boundary-margin discussion. The related-work narrative and positioning against latency attacks and existing defenses otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and substantially reorganized: v1 Sections 6–11 become Appendices A–F after the references, and the conclusion moves into a six-section main paper. Most prose is retained, alongside minor wording corrections, expanded author contact information, and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The single-column document becomes a two-column main paper and supplement, extensively resizing and relocating figures, tables, and algorithms. All 12 figures and five tables remain; Figures 9–12 and Tables 2–5 move into the supplement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful source-code access information and supporting citations, while separating the main argument from the retained supplementary evidence. These provide modest gains in documentation and organization. The denser layout makes several figures smaller, and the scientific methods, results, and validation remain unchanged.
